observation_summary: The generated JavaScript code contains raw null characters, which causes some browsers (like IE9) to incorrectly terminate script parsing.
reasoning_summary: The code generator was failing to explicitly handle the null character ('\0') when serializing strings. As a result, it was outputting the literal null character (U+0000) into the generated JavaScript code instead of an escaped representation (like '\0'). This caused issues in certain environments, such as IE9, which interpreted the raw null character as an end-of-file marker, prematurely terminating script execution.
